cards.explanation: The answer is that they hope to catch Jesus in His words. The text says the spies were hoping to catch Him in His words in order to hand Him over to the governor (Luke 20:20). Everything else about them is costume, friends: the polite faces, the sweet talk, the whole act. It's a trap wearing its Sunday best.

The answer is that they ask whether it is lawful to pay taxes to Caesar. The text says, “Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?” (Luke 20:22). Taxes, friends. Even my mustache gets nervous at that word. And notice they only give Him two choices, yes or no.

The answer is True. The text says, “But Jesus saw through their duplicity…” (Luke 20:23). Duplicity means two faces, one sweet and one sneaky. The spies practiced that smile for a while, I bet, and it didn't matter one bit.

The answer is “Caesar’s.” Jesus asked whose image and inscription were on the denarius, and the answer was right there on the coin (Luke 20:24). Think about that, friends. The spies are the ones answering, and their own answer sets up what Jesus says next.

The answer is that Jesus tells them to give Caesar what is his and God what is His. He says, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.” (Luke 20:25) He asks them to show Him a denarius, then answers them with it. It's a short answer, friends, and it doesn't leave the spies much to grab onto. I wish my answers landed like that when somebody asks me if the cookies are done.

The answer is False, and the text is clear: “And they were unable to trap Him in His words before the people.” (Luke 20:26) Then it adds that they were amazed at His answer and fell silent. They set the trap, and it never closed. I know that feeling, friends. I once built a cookie pyramid, and it also did not go as planned.
The answer is True. Luke 20:27 calls them the Sadducees, “…who say there is no resurrection…” Then they come to question Him about it. They walk in with their position already baked, friends.

The answer is that the living brother marries the widow and raises children for his brother. The Sadducees say Moses wrote that “…the man is to marry his brother’s widow and raise up offspring for him.” (Luke 20:28) So the living brother steps in for the one who died. It's a lot to ask, friends, but that's what they quote.

The answer is none of them. The Sadducees say the first one “died childless,” and then that “…all seven died, leaving no children.” (Luke 20:29, 31) Seven brothers is a lot to keep track of, friends, so here's the easy number: zero. It's a sad story, and it sets up the question they bring to Jesus.

The answer is wife. The Sadducees ask, “So then, in the resurrection, whose wife will she be? For all seven were married to her.” (Luke 20:33) Seven marriages, one woman, one question. My head hurts just counting, friends.

The answer is False. Jesus says those considered worthy to share in the age to come and in the resurrection “…will neither marry nor be given in marriage.” (Luke 20:35) That's the age to come, and He sets it apart from this age. This is a hard thing the Sadducees asked, friends, and Jesus answers it right there.

The answer is that they can no longer die because they are like the angels. Jesus says, “…they can no longer die, because they are like the angels.” (Luke 20:36) The reason is given right there in the verse. I'd call that a pretty big promise, friends.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “And since they are sons of the resurrection, they are sons of God.” (Luke 20:36) Coming from a stamper who once lived in a junk drawer, friends, that hits me right in the mustache. It's good news.

The answer is living. Jesus says, “He is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for to Him all are alive.” (Luke 20:38) He points to Moses, who calls the Lord “the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” (Luke 20:37) That's how Jesus answers the Sadducees, using Moses himself.

The answer is that they don't dare question Him any further. The text says, “And they did not dare to question Him any further.” (Luke 20:40) Nobody is out of questions, friends. They just don't dare to ask Him more.
